articles.title: Stop The Presses, Link Can Jump In Ocarina Of Time Remake
articles.summary: Today, Nintendo aired The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. We learned the Ocarina of Time remake is launching November 5. We heard about a new orchestra concert touring the world in 2027.
body: At one point, the younger version of Link comes across a pond with rocks that he must jump across. In the previous Ocarina of Time game, Link would automatically jump when approaching the rocks. Now, however, players can make Link jump whenever they like, at the press of a button.

As Aonuma himself pointed out in the demo, jumping may not seem like a big deal, but because the original game didn't allow for free jumping, this is a major change in the context of Ocarina of Time. Though what was shown was faithful to the original, the combination of this jump mechanic and the new sprint mechanic could lead to some changes in level design in the final game.

The gameplay demo also showed off the remake's updated visual style through multiple locations from the Nintendo 64 classic, including the Deku Tree, Hyrule Market, and Kokiri Forest. Aonuma also revealed new Ocarina mechanics, including the ability to hum a tune or play it on a physical instrument and have it register through the Switch 2's built-in microphone.
points: Today, Nintendo aired The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct.
We learned the Ocarina of Time remake is launching November 5.
We heard about a new orchestra concert touring the world in 2027.
In the previous Ocarina of Time game, Link would automatically jump when approaching the rocks.
articles.author: Jason Fanelli

articles.title: The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct Missed A Giant Wind Waker-Sized Opportunity
articles.summary: If you were hoping to see older Zelda games ported to or remastered for the Switch at the recent Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, you were likely disappointed, as Nintendo instead dedicated almost the entire show to its upcoming Ocarina of Time remake.
body: Out of all the Legend of Zelda remasters that have come to Switch consoles over the years, there's still a sizable Wind Waker HD-shaped hole in that collection. The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker HD released on the Wii U in 2013, with a number of upgrades compared to the original 2003 GameCube version.

While the original version of Wind Waker was added to the Switch Online GameCube library last year, the Wii U version is much better in comparison. It provides a smoother experience with various quality-of-life improvements, like a resolution boost, faster loading times, and subtle changes to the game that make it less of a chore to play in its second half. While it isn't considered as influential as Ocarina of Time, Wind Waker's impact can still be felt in modern Zelda games today.
The fact then that the upgraded version of one of the best Zelda games of all time is still only available on the Wii U is a shame. Much the same could be said of Twilight Princess HD on the Wii U.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Release Date Confirmed, and It Looks Like a Faithful-Looking Return With a Few Surprises
articles.summary: Nintendo has finally shown off its upcoming The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and revealed it will launch on November 5. Yes, Nintendo is launching a big video game in the same month as Grand Theft Auto 6 — and is one of the very few publishers seemingly happy to risk doing so.
body: This new version of Nintendo's legendary N64 adventure has been remade from the ground-up for Switch 2, with a remarkable new 3D visual style that looks quite unlike any other Zelda game in the past. Other more modern advancements have also been made, such as being able to manually jump, dash, quickly switch between items, or aim via motion controls.
A new menu feature, the Threads of Time, will act as a quest log and a tapestry-like showcase of your exploits so far.

The main structure of the game appears to be largely unchanged, and different regions of Hyrule remain distinct areas with loading screens as you pass between them. A few extra areas were teased in places like Castle Town, with minigames within shops.
For everything else shown today, including news on the upcoming live-action Legend of Zelda movie, catch up on everything shown during the Legend of Zelda Nintendo Direct right here.

articles.title: The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Looks Fantastic In First Gameplay Look
articles.summary: After months of rumors, Nintendo finally revealed that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was real back in June. While that reveal was purely cinematic, today's Nintendo Direct for The Legend of Zelda showed off gameplay for the remake and offered a closer look at its updated art…
body: The Switch 2 exclusive stays true to the 1998 original's aesthetics, while showcasing a huge upgrade visually. Link's hat and tunic, for example, showcase detailed threading and embroidering, along with berries on his cap. The lighting system looks fantastic, too, as sunlight pokes through the forest as Link heads to the Great Deku Tree.

As for gameplay, players will have a button for Link to jump and dash. That may sound silly to younger people who grew up on The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, but it's a huge change from the Nintendo 64 title. How the jump button could possibly impact dungeon design wasn't addressed but should prove interesting later this year.

Overall, the first gameplay revealed for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake seemed to address a lot of my concerns of a simple remaster for the game. The Switch 2 title seems faithful while still altering enough for modern audiences--and those of us who played the original (or 3DS remaster) plenty of times already.

articles.title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Borrows At Least One Mechanic From Breath Of The Wild
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 looks like a very faithful remake of the Nintendo 64 classic, but as seen in the Zelda 40th anniversary Direct, this updated version of the game takes at least one element from the modern open-world Zelda games.
body: When demonstrating the returning Fairy Slingshot item, Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma showed off the weapon-switching and aiming mechanics, which look nearly identical to the same systems in Breath of the Wild.

Players can quickly swap their weapons in a horizontal menu similar to the one used in Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, and Echoes of Wisdom. Aiming a projectile weapon also uses the same reticle seen in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, with full motion control support as well. The difference in Ocarina is that you can use Z-targeting in conjunction with free aim.

Upon the official announcement of the Ocarina of Time remake, speculation amongst the Zelda fanbase ran rampant about whether the new title would remain faithful to the original game or reimagine it to be similar to modern Zelda titles. While Aonuma made it clear from the beginning of his presentation that Nintendo is taking the former approach, it looks like there will at least be some UI and quality-of-life elements taken from recent games.

articles.title: Nintendo Reveals Lego Link & Epona Set for The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary
articles.summary: Nintendo has revealed an Ocarina of Time-themed Lego Link & Epona set as part of its The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. The set was unveiled along with a series of other events, merchandise, and more that the company is set to roll out through the rest of 2026 and part of 2027.
body: You can see a first look at the Lego Link and Epona set below.

Nintendo revealed additional details about its new The Legend of Zelda Lego in a press release following today's Direct. It confirmed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – Link & Epona is a 1,750-piece set and described it as a "collectible display model for adults."
It is expected to launch spring 2027. Its price, unfortunately, has not been revealed, but sets like these can typically be pretty expensive.

The two The Legend of Zelda Lego releases Nintendo has launched previously may offer a bit of insight into just how much Link & Epona will cost. The Ocarina of Time - The Final Battle set, which features minifigs for Link and Zelda, as well as a full-size Ganon build, is 1,003 pieces and is priced at $129.99. The much larger 2-in-1 Great Deku Tree is 2,500 pieces and is priced at a whopping $299.99.

articles.title: Call of Duty 2 Signaled the Beginning of the End of Halo's Reign As the King of Console Shooters
articles.summary: Call of Duty 2 was, quite simply, the right game at the right time for Xbox 360. It showed gamers what the new console was capable of while also being a stellar game regardless of platform.
body: This is an IGN opinion piece from Ryan McCaffrey, who worked at Official Xbox Magazine from 2002-2012 during the original Xbox and Xbox 360 era before joining IGN, where he remains “the Xbox guy.” In the run-up to Xbox’s 25th anniversary, he’ll be sharing his memories from the platform’s first quarter-century.

Younger readers might not remember a time when Call of Duty wasn't one of the biggest franchises in all of gaming, but I promise you that there was a time. I had played the original on PC — the only platform it had been released on — back in 2003. And, yes, I quite liked it. It was an excellent World War 2-set military first-person shooter.

My eager but not feverish anticipation for Call of Duty 2 changed when I got to go to Infinity Ward in the summer of 2005 to do a cover story on Infinity Ward's sequel. And I remember very clearly what jumped out at my first as I was shown an early mission from the campaign: the volumetric smoke effects. With the increased horsepower of the Xbox 360, smoke grenades mattered more than ever during gameplay, as tossing them to obscure the enemy's vision while you darted across the path nearby Axis a-holes was integrated into the mission design.
points: Call of Duty 2 was, quite simply, the right game at the right time for Xbox 360.
It showed gamers what the new console was capable of while also being a stellar game regardless of platform.

articles.title: 5 Things Completely New to the Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
articles.summary: Nintendo gave players their first in-depth look at gameplay for the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake during today's Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. While the game's new graphical style got a lot of attention (love it or hate it), the company also revealed a number of new features.
body: Link can jump whenever he wants now. This might not sound like a big deal, but Nintendo made a big show of Link's newfound freedom. In the original Ocarina of Time, Link automatically jumped when he ran close to an edge, but outside that context he was largely bound to the ground. No more! Jumping is now bound to the X button and is one of the many ways Nintendo is making the nearly three-decade-old game more inline with modern gaming expectations. Furthermore, he can dash by holding down the A button. This is an improvement over the original game's strategy of rolling to speed traversal along.

Taking a page from Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, you can swap items with one button in the Ocarina of Time remake. The original game allowed some items to be assigned to buttons for easy access, but everything else had to be equipped by pausing the game. Now Link can cycle through all of his items with a simple button press. It might not be a glamorous new feature, but it sure does streamline the game and means you'll spend way less time in menus now.
points: Nintendo gave players their first in-depth look at gameplay for the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake during today's Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda Live-Action Movie Will Be an Original Story Based on the Series So Far
articles.summary: Nintendo has discussed further details of its live-action The Legend of Zelda movie, including its title and story. Revealed during today's The Legend of Zelda-dedicated Nintendo Direct by Shigeru Miyamoto, we learned that (unsurprisingly) the film's title will be: The Legend of Zelda.
body: As for the film's story, Miyamoto said that it would be based on stories and concepts from the franchise so far. In other words, don't expect this to be a direct adaptation of a particular game.
Otherwise, details on the movie remain thin on the ground (and sadly, there's no sign of Tingle just yet).

Originally announced in 2023, The Legend of Zelda is helmed by Maze Runner and Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes director Wes Ball, while Nintendo's legendary Shigeru Miyamoto is listed as a co-producer, alongside Marvel production veteran Avi Arad. The movie was shot last winter in New Zealand, with the Middle-earth-like location now doubling for Hyrule.
The Legend of Zelda is currently set to arrive on April 30, 2027.

body: Here's how to help Vicho and find the culprit in The Blood of Dawnwalker 's "A Study in Crimson" quest.

To obtain "A Study in Crimson" in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you must find Vicho. This quest isn't marked on your map, but the citizens of Svartrau City may have mentioned a "curio emporium" in passing. If you find, enter, and investigate this mysterious shop, "A Study in Crimson" will begin.
Beware that "A Study in Crimson" costs four time segments in total and can only be completed at night. If you run out of time, Vicho will ask you to come back the following night.

articles.title: Battlefield 6 Redsec is borrowing yet another mode from Call of Duty: Warzone - Resurgence
articles.summary: It's been argued that Battlefield 6 's Redsec battle royale off-shoot is a response to Call of Duty's popular Warzone mode, and today's news is another indication of that.
body: Battlefield Studios has unveiled Rapid Royale, Redsec's version of Warzone's Resurgence. If you're unfamiliar, Resurgence takes place on dedicated maps that are far smaller than the main mode's large playground, and offers many ways to respawn after death. The pace is significantly faster with more frequent firefights as a result, and these are the principles guiding the Redsec version, too.

Rapid Royale features a reduced player count and is likewise only available on maps smaller than the main mode's. The circles move faster, too, further pushing players closer and closer together. Expect matches that finish quickly, notably a lot shorter than the main mode.

Rapid Royale is one of several new additions coming to Battlefield 6 and Redsec with Season 5, which does not yet have a release date. While we wait for that, Season 4's final stage - named Tidal Strike - kicks off 15th September and introduces the first iteration of proximity chat.

As the name suggests, the feature allows players to communicate with others around them who are not part of their squad. It's initially available only in battle royale, with the plan to expand it to Battlefield 6 multiplayer down the road.
points: It's been argued that Battlefield 6 's Redsec battle royale off-shoot is a response to Call of Duty's popular Warzone mode, and today's news is another indication of that.

articles.title: Zelda Direct: Every Big Ocarina of Time Reveal and Trailer from Nintendo
articles.summary: Nintendo hosted a 30-minute-long Zelda Direct honoring The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary. It's the first of two Nintendo Directs this week, and while the Ocarina of Time remake had plenty of time in the spotlight, there were a few other announcements as well.
body: Below, we've rounded up all the major Zelda Direct announcements and reveals.

Zelda creator Shigeru Miyamoto said you'll understand why the film has no subtitle after you see it. Miyamoto teased homages to the series and a big role for the Triforce, the latter of which is hardly surprising since it's a series cornerstone. You can catch the film in theaters on April 30, 2027, and Miyamoto said future updates about the film will be shared via Nintendo Today.
Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma showed off a look at the Ocarina of Time remake, specifically the early Kokiri Forest, and the release date. It's out on Nov. 5.

Aonuma gave a brief explanation of why the graphics look the way they do. Aonuma also teased a few new features, including minor-but-impossible-for-the-Nintendo64 changes like adding a jump button, letting you rotate the camera, and, a rather more interesting one, the ability to swim and dive without special clothing.

articles.title: Nintendo and Lego Officially Reveal New 'Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time' Set
articles.summary: The next collaboration set between Lego and Nintendo is a neat one. Timed for release after theupcoming Ocarina of Time remake, Nintendo announced during its The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct that the next Legend of Zelda Lego set will be themed around Link and Epona.
body: Adult Link sits atop his horse Epona while wielding the Master Sword and the Hylian Shield. Epona rears back into a dramatic pose that calls to mind Jacques-Louis David's famous painting Napoleon Crossing the Alps. The remaining details around the upcoming Link & Epona set have not been revealed, including its price and piece count. Based on the released image, it seems both Link and Epona will have posable leg joints.
The Lego The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – Link & Epona set is built from 1,750 pieces, and will be available starting spring 2027.

Nintendo and Lego have had a fruitful partnership in recent years. Earlier this year, they released Ocarina of Time - The Final Battle, a 1,003-piece set that features Link and Zelda dueling with Ganon in a recreation of Ocarina of Time 's iconic ultimate boss fight. That one went for a hefty $129.99. Before that, there was the even pricier Deku Tree set, a roughly $300, 2,500-piece mega build that has since been retired after selling out. It seems fair to assume that the Link & Epona set will be cheaper than its predecessors, as it looks a bit smaller in scale.
points: The next collaboration set between Lego and Nintendo is a neat one.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake gameplay finally revealed during 40th anniversary Nintendo Direct, and it looks… interesting
articles.summary: Gameplay has been released for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake at long last during today's Zelda 40th anniversary Nintendo Direct. It'll be releasing on the Nintendo Switch 2 on the 5th November.
body: The gameplay, narrated by producer Eiji Aonuma, shows what looks to be a largely faithful recreation of the original 3rd person adventure classic, albeit with some modern advancements. For one, Link can jump manually now, and the whole game has been brought to life in a new engine.

A lot of classic sounds and animations also appear to have been either brought over untouched, or recreated faithfully. The famous chest opening animation, for example, looks very much the same as it did all those years ago. Just with that newer aesthetic applied to it.

Some new features for the game worth highlighting: Link can now jump, swim and dive underwater, he can swap between items with single button, characters are fully voiced in cutscenes, Hyrule Castle Town has some new areas previously closed off, you can dash to move faster, time of day now progresses in real-time everywhere. Nintendo, interestingly, says the new game still has loading screens to maintin the feeling of the original.

A particularly cool feature was also shown in regards to playing Link's iconic ocarina. Players can turn on their microphone and hum, whistle, or sing the various tunes required for gameplay changes to occur.
points: Gameplay has been released for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake at long last during today's Zelda 40th anniversary Nintendo Direct.
It'll be releasing on the Nintendo Switch 2 on the 5th November.

articles.title: Everything announced at Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct
articles.summary: Can you believe it? Link (the green one) is 40 this year, yet his boundless enthusiasm for adventure still hasn't waned. My boundless enthusiasm, meanwhile, waned decades back, so it's clearly something in the Hyrule air.
body: That, we now know, included a full reveal for its Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake following its somewhat controversial unveiling earlier this year, a new Zelda-themed Switch 2, a couple of amiibo, a musical tour, and more. For the full rundown of announcements, cast your eyes below...

A classic reborn, and all of that. Not everyone loved the semi-realistic look Nintendo appeared to be going for when it unveiled Switch 2's Ocarina of Time remake earlier this year. But we've now had a chance to see it properly in action, and it's certainly different, opting for a moody, misty, fairytale vibe unlike any Zelda we've seen before.

New features include a manual jump and the ability to hum ocarina tunes into the Switch 2's mic rather than tapping them out. Or you could toot a tune on an actual ocarina if you have one lying around. It's fully voiced too (which is going to take some getting used to), and supports Zelda Notes on the Switch app. As for when it's out, it's coming 5th November this year.
points: Link (the green one) is 40 this year, yet his boundless enthusiasm for adventure still hasn't waned.
My boundless enthusiasm, meanwhile, waned decades back, so it's clearly something in the Hyrule air.

Arjun comes to Street Fighter 6 on October 13th for PlayStation 4 (PS4), PlayStation 5 (PS5), PC (Steam), Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X|S!

body: A mobile battle for the ages as we compare the same games running on Switch 2 in mobile mode up against iPhone 17 Pro. Switch 2 has the advantage of more specific optimisation from developers and active cooling at the expense of form factor and a much less efficient process node.
